name: Porter's Five Forces
one_line_summary: Industry profitability shaped by buyers, suppliers, entrants, substitutes, and rivalry.

name: Porter's Generic Strategies
one_line_summary: Cost leadership, differentiation, and focus as the three viable competitive postures.

name: Porter's Value Chain
one_line_summary: Decomposes the firm into primary and support activities to locate sources of value.

name: BCG Growth-Share Matrix
one_line_summary: Classifies business units as Stars, Cash Cows, Question Marks, or Dogs.

name: GE-McKinsey Nine-Box Matrix
one_line_summary: Portfolio prioritization on industry attractiveness vs business unit strength.

name: Ansoff Matrix
one_line_summary: Maps growth strategies across existing/new products and existing/new markets.

name: McKinsey 7S Framework
one_line_summary: Aligns strategy, structure, systems, shared values, skills, style, and staff.

name: Blue Ocean Strategy
one_line_summary: Create uncontested market space rather than compete in saturated 'red oceans.'

name: Disruptive Innovation Theory
one_line_summary: Low-end and new-market entrants displace incumbents serving overshot customers.

name: Jobs to Be Done
one_line_summary: Customers 'hire' products to make progress on a job in a context.

name: Lean Startup
one_line_summary: Build-measure-learn loops with validated learning under extreme uncertainty.

name: Business Model Canvas
one_line_summary: Nine-block visual schema for describing and iterating a business model.

name: Value Proposition Canvas
one_line_summary: Aligns customer pains, gains, and jobs to product features and benefits.

name: Lean Canvas
one_line_summary: Maurya's adaptation of the BMC for early-stage startups under high uncertainty.

name: OKRs
one_line_summary: Ambitious objectives paired with measurable key results, popularized by Grove and Doerr.

name: Balanced Scorecard
one_line_summary: Performance measurement across financial, customer, internal process, and learning perspectives.

name: Wardley Mapping
one_line_summary: Strategy via value-chain components plotted against evolutionary maturity.

name: Theory of Constraints
one_line_summary: System throughput is governed by its single binding constraint at any time.

name: Toyota Production System
one_line_summary: Eliminate waste through just-in-time, jidoka, and continuous improvement.

name: Six Sigma
one_line_summary: Reduce defects to 3.4 per million through statistical process control and DMAIC.

name: Kaizen
one_line_summary: Continuous incremental improvement involving everyone in an organization.

name: Hoshin Kanri
one_line_summary: Cascading strategy deployment with catchball alignment between levels.

name: Kotter's 8-Step Change Model
one_line_summary: Sequential change leadership steps from urgency through anchoring in culture.

name: Lewin's Change Model
one_line_summary: Three-stage model of behavioral change at individual or organizational level.

name: ADKAR
one_line_summary: Awareness, Desire, Knowledge, Ability, Reinforcement — Prosci's individual-change model.

name: Bridges' Transition Model
one_line_summary: Distinguishes external change from internal psychological transition through endings, neutral zone, beginnings.

name: Greiner's Growth Model
one_line_summary: Predictable phases of organizational growth punctuated by crises.

name: Tuckman's Stages
one_line_summary: Stage model of small-group development including the later-added 'adjourning.'
band_notes: Widely cited but limited rigorous empirical validation of discrete stages.

name: Theory X and Theory Y
one_line_summary: McGregor's contrasting assumptions about whether workers inherently dislike or seek work.
band_notes: Useful framing of managerial assumptions; not empirically validated as a typology.

name: Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory
one_line_summary: Distinguishes hygiene factors that prevent dissatisfaction from motivators that drive satisfaction.
band_notes: Influential but the two-factor structure has not been replicated in subsequent research.

name: Hofstede's Cultural Dimensions
one_line_summary: Six dimensions for comparing national cultures, originally derived from IBM survey data.
band_notes: Influential but methodologically critiqued; original sample (IBM employees) and dimensional structure have been challenged.

name: Trompenaars' Cultural Dimensions
one_line_summary: Alternative cross-cultural framework emphasizing relationships, time, and environment.

name: Management by Objectives
one_line_summary: Drucker's approach: align managers and employees through agreed measurable objectives.

name: Mintzberg's Management Roles
one_line_summary: Ten managerial roles grouped as interpersonal, informational, and decisional.

name: Mintzberg's Configurations
one_line_summary: Five organizational structures from simple to adhocracy, defined by coordination mechanism.

name: SWOT Analysis
one_line_summary: Surfaces strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats for a venture or decision.

name: PESTLE Analysis
one_line_summary: Scans Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal, and Environmental factors.

name: VRIO Framework
one_line_summary: Tests resources for Value, Rarity, Imitability, and Organization to find sustained advantage.

name: Resource-Based View
one_line_summary: Competitive advantage stems from valuable, rare, inimitable, organized internal resources.

name: Dynamic Capabilities
one_line_summary: Teece's view of advantage from sensing, seizing, and reconfiguring assets in changing environments.

name: Stakeholder Theory
one_line_summary: Freeman's argument that firms must serve all affected parties, not just shareholders.

name: Triple Bottom Line
one_line_summary: Performance measured across people, planet, and profit dimensions.

name: Three Horizons Model
one_line_summary: McKinsey portfolio model balancing core, emerging, and exploratory growth initiatives.

name: Holacracy
one_line_summary: Self-management system replacing traditional hierarchy with distributed authority and circles.

name: Sociocracy
one_line_summary: Consent-based governance through linked circles of decision-making.

name: Pyramid Principle
one_line_summary: Top-down communication structure starting with the answer, supported by grouped arguments.

name: Strategy Canvas
one_line_summary: Blue Ocean visual contrasting an industry's value-curve to identify reinvention opportunities.

name: RACI Matrix
one_line_summary: Clarifies who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted, and Informed for each task.

name: DACI
one_line_summary: Driver, Approver, Contributors, Informed — decision-roles variant of RACI.

name: Eisenhower Matrix
one_line_summary: Sorts tasks into four quadrants by urgency and importance.

name: MoSCoW
one_line_summary: Prioritizes requirements as Must, Should, Could, or Won't have.

name: RICE Scoring
one_line_summary: Prioritizes features by Reach, Impact, Confidence, and Effort.

name: ICE Scoring
one_line_summary: Prioritizes ideas on Impact, Confidence, and Ease — simpler RICE precursor.

name: Kano Model
one_line_summary: Classifies features as basic, performance, or delighters by their effect on customer satisfaction.

name: Pareto Analysis
one_line_summary: Identifies the vital few inputs accounting for the majority of outputs.

name: Pugh Matrix
one_line_summary: Concept selection by scoring alternatives against weighted criteria relative to a baseline.

name: After Action Review
one_line_summary: Structured reflection on what was intended, what happened, why, and what to do next.

name: Premortem
one_line_summary: Imagine the project has failed and work backward to prevent the causes.

name: Five Whys
one_line_summary: Iteratively ask 'why' to drill from symptom to root cause, originating in Toyota's TPS.

name: Fishbone Diagram
one_line_summary: Visual root-cause analysis grouping causes under categories like people, process, materials.

name: Six Thinking Hats
one_line_summary: De Bono's parallel-thinking method using six distinct perspective 'hats.'

name: Lateral Thinking
one_line_summary: De Bono's approach to generating ideas by deliberately disrupting linear logic.

name: SCAMPER
one_line_summary: Idea-generation prompts: Substitute, Combine, Adapt, Modify, Put to other use, Eliminate, Reverse.

name: TRIZ
one_line_summary: Altshuller's pattern-based system for technical innovation, drawn from millions of patents.

name: Mind Mapping
one_line_summary: Buzan's radial visual technique for non-linear note-taking and brainstorming.

name: Affinity Diagram
one_line_summary: Group disparate ideas into emergent themes by intuitive sorting.

name: Force Field Analysis
one_line_summary: Lewin's mapping of driving and restraining forces around a proposed change.

name: Decision Tree Analysis
one_line_summary: Branching diagram of choices, chance events, and outcomes with associated values.

name: Stage-Gate Process
one_line_summary: Cooper's product-development model with go/kill decisions between defined stages.

name: DMAIC
one_line_summary: Six Sigma improvement cycle: Define, Measure, Analyze, Improve, Control.

name: DMADV
one_line_summary: Six Sigma design cycle: Define, Measure, Analyze, Design, Verify.

name: Total Quality Management
one_line_summary: Organization-wide focus on continuous quality improvement with customer at the center.

name: Quality Function Deployment
one_line_summary: Translates customer requirements into engineering specifications via matrix analysis.

name: Poka-Yoke
one_line_summary: Design constraints that make errors impossible or immediately obvious.

name: Hedgehog Concept
one_line_summary: Collins' intersection of passion, economic engine, and what-you-can-be-best-at.

name: Level 5 Leadership
one_line_summary: Collins' hierarchy of executive capability culminating in humility plus fierce resolve.

name: Five Dysfunctions of a Team
one_line_summary: Lencioni's pyramid: absence of trust, fear of conflict, lack of commitment, avoidance of accountability, inattention to results.

name: Situational Leadership
one_line_summary: Hersey-Blanchard model matching leadership style to follower readiness.

name: Servant Leadership
one_line_summary: Greenleaf's leadership philosophy where the leader's primary role is to serve.

name: Transformational Leadership
one_line_summary: Bass and Burns model emphasizing inspiration, intellectual stimulation, and individualized consideration.

name: 4Ps of Marketing
one_line_summary: McCarthy's product, price, place, promotion as the four levers of marketing.

name: 7Ps of Marketing
one_line_summary: Booms and Bitner's extension adding people, process, and physical evidence for services.

name: 4Cs of Marketing
one_line_summary: Lauterborn's customer-centric reframe: consumer, cost, convenience, communication.

name: AIDA
one_line_summary: Attention, Interest, Desire, Action — classic linear advertising response model.

name: AIDAS
one_line_summary: AIDA extended with Satisfaction to capture post-purchase loyalty.

name: STP
one_line_summary: Sequential approach: segment market, target chosen segments, position offering distinctively.

name: Marketing Funnel
one_line_summary: Awareness through purchase as a narrowing pipeline of prospects.

name: Pirate Metrics
one_line_summary: McClure's Acquisition, Activation, Retention, Referral, Revenue lifecycle for startups.

name: Crossing the Chasm
one_line_summary: Moore's adaptation showing the gap between early adopters and early majority.

name: Diffusion of Innovations
one_line_summary: Rogers' S-curve model of how innovations spread through innovators, adopters, and laggards.

name: StoryBrand
one_line_summary: Donald Miller's seven-part brand-narrative framework casting customer as hero, brand as guide.

name: Net Promoter Score
one_line_summary: Single-question loyalty measure based on likelihood to recommend.

name: Customer Lifetime Value
one_line_summary: Projected revenue from a customer relationship over its entire duration.

name: RFM Analysis
one_line_summary: Customer segmentation by how recently, how often, and how much they purchased.

name: Means-End Theory
one_line_summary: Links product attributes to consumer values through a chain of consequences.

name: Ehrenberg-Bass Laws
one_line_summary: Empirical regularities in buying behavior, including double jeopardy and brand penetration.

name: Customer Journey Mapping
one_line_summary: Visualizes a customer's stages, touchpoints, emotions, and pain points across an experience.

name: Empathy Map
one_line_summary: Visual organizing what a user says, thinks, does, and feels.

name: Personas
one_line_summary: Composite fictional representatives of target user segments used to ground design and marketing.

name: Hooked Model
one_line_summary: Eyal's trigger-action-reward-investment loop for habit-forming products.

name: Fogg Behavior Model
one_line_summary: Behavior occurs when motivation, ability, and prompt converge simultaneously.

name: Big Five
one_line_summary: Five dimensions of personality: Openness, Conscientiousness, Extraversion, Agreeableness, Neuroticism.

name: HEXACO
one_line_summary: Six-factor personality model adding Honesty-Humility to the Big Five.

name: Myers-Briggs Type Indicator
one_line_summary: Sixteen personality types from Jungian dichotomies; widely used despite weak psychometric support.
band_notes: Weak psychometric reliability and validity; rejected by mainstream personality psychology despite cultural penetration. Bimodal forced-choice on continuously distributed traits.

name: Enneagram
one_line_summary: Nine interconnected personality types with wings, instincts, and integration arrows.
band_notes: Origins in Gurdjieff/Ichazo esoteric traditions; no peer-reviewed empirical validation. Often presented as if psychometrically validated when it is not.

name: DISC Assessment
one_line_summary: Behavioral typology along Dominance, Influence, Steadiness, and Conscientiousness.
band_notes: Modest psychometric support; substantially weaker than Five-Factor instruments.

name: CliftonStrengths
one_line_summary: Gallup's 34 talent themes used for strengths-based development.
band_notes: Validation primarily from Gallup (proprietor); limited independent replication.

name: Hogan Personality Inventory
one_line_summary: Workplace personality assessment grounded in the Five-Factor Model.

name: Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs
one_line_summary: Pyramid from physiological needs through self-actualization, with self-transcendence later added.
band_notes: Core needs categories are useful but the strict hierarchy structure is not empirically supported.

name: Self-Determination Theory
one_line_summary: Deci and Ryan's framework of autonomy, competence, and relatedness as basic psychological needs.

name: Attachment Theory
one_line_summary: Bowlby and Ainsworth's framework of early bonds shaping internal working models of relationships.

name: Bowen Family Systems Theory
one_line_summary: Family as an emotional unit shaped by differentiation, triangles, and multigenerational transmission.
band_notes: Clinically influential; limited rigorous empirical validation.

name: Internal Family Systems
one_line_summary: Schwartz's parts-based therapy model with managers, exiles, firefighters, and the Self.
band_notes: Emerging clinical support but evidence base remains thinner than CBT or DBT.

name: Polyvagal Theory
one_line_summary: Porges' theory of three vagal pathways governing safety, mobilization, and shutdown.
band_notes: Therapeutic adoption is broad but underlying neurophysiology has been seriously challenged in mainstream physiology (Grossman and others).

name: Transactional Analysis
one_line_summary: Berne's framework of Parent, Adult, and Child ego states transacting in relationships.
band_notes: Some clinical use; limited contemporary empirical validation.

name: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy
one_line_summary: Beck's framework linking thoughts, feelings, and behaviors as targets for change.

name: Dialectical Behavior Therapy
one_line_summary: Linehan's CBT extension adding mindfulness, distress tolerance, and emotion regulation.

name: Acceptance and Commitment Therapy
one_line_summary: Hayes' framework using acceptance and values clarification rather than symptom reduction.

name: Rational Emotive Behavior Therapy
one_line_summary: Ellis' precursor to CBT focused on disputing irrational beliefs.

name: Schema Therapy
one_line_summary: Young's integrative therapy targeting early maladaptive schemas formed in childhood.

name: Jungian Analytical Psychology
one_line_summary: Jung's framework of personal and collective unconscious, archetypes, and individuation.
band_notes: Influential in depth psychology and culture; not validated within empirical psychology.

name: Jungian Archetypes
one_line_summary: Universal symbolic patterns including Self, Shadow, Anima/Animus, Hero, Mother.
band_notes: Not empirically grounded; useful as cultural and narrative scaffolding rather than psychological taxonomy.

name: King Warrior Magician Lover
one_line_summary: Moore and Gillette's masculine archetypes drawn from depth psychology.
band_notes: Derived from Jungian depth psychology; valuable for self-development work but not empirically validated.

name: Erikson's Stages
one_line_summary: Eight psychosocial stages from trust vs mistrust through integrity vs despair.

name: Piaget's Stages
one_line_summary: Four stages of cognitive development from sensorimotor through formal operations.

name: Kohlberg's Stages of Moral Development
one_line_summary: Six stages across pre-conventional, conventional, and post-conventional moral reasoning.

name: Zone of Proximal Development
one_line_summary: Vygotsky's gap between what a learner can do alone and with guidance.

name: Social Learning Theory
one_line_summary: Bandura's account of learning through observation, modeling, and imitation.

name: Self-Efficacy Theory
one_line_summary: Bandura's construct: belief in one's ability to execute behaviors needed for outcomes.

name: Locus of Control
one_line_summary: Rotter's dimension contrasting internal vs external attribution of control over events.

name: Learned Helplessness
one_line_summary: Seligman's account of passivity arising from repeated uncontrollable aversive events.

name: Positive Psychology
one_line_summary: Seligman's flourishing framework: Positive emotion, Engagement, Relationships, Meaning, Accomplishment.

name: Flow Theory
one_line_summary: Csikszentmihalyi's optimal experience at the balance of challenge and skill.

name: Dual-Process Theory
one_line_summary: Two modes of cognition: fast intuitive and slow deliberative, popularized by Kahneman.

name: Cognitive Dissonance Theory
one_line_summary: Festinger's account of discomfort from holding contradictory beliefs and motivated rationalization.

name: Theory of Planned Behavior
one_line_summary: Ajzen's model: intention shaped by attitudes, norms, and perceived control.

name: Health Belief Model
one_line_summary: Health behavior driven by perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits, and barriers.

name: Transtheoretical Model
one_line_summary: Prochaska and DiClemente's stages: precontemplation, contemplation, preparation, action, maintenance.

name: Motivational Interviewing
one_line_summary: Miller and Rollnick's collaborative method for evoking change talk and resolving ambivalence.

name: Trauma-Informed Care
one_line_summary: Approach assuming widespread trauma and prioritizing safety, choice, collaboration, empowerment.

name: Job Demands-Resources Model
one_line_summary: Demerouti and Bakker's framework explaining burnout and engagement at work.

name: Conservation of Resources Theory
one_line_summary: Hobfoll's stress theory: people seek to acquire and protect valued resources.

name: Broaden-and-Build Theory
one_line_summary: Fredrickson's theory that positive emotions broaden thought-action repertoires.

name: Karpman Drama Triangle
one_line_summary: Three relational roles in conflict: Persecutor, Victim, Rescuer.
band_notes: Clinically useful schema; not empirically tested as a falsifiable theory.

name: Choice Theory
one_line_summary: Glasser's framework of human behavior driven by five basic needs.
band_notes: Glasser's framework has practitioner adoption but limited rigorous empirical research.

name: Gottman Sound Relationship House
one_line_summary: Empirically derived model of healthy couple relationships across nine levels.

name: Adlerian Individual Psychology
one_line_summary: Adler's framework emphasizing inferiority, social interest, and lifestyle.
band_notes: Influential in counseling traditions; limited contemporary empirical research.

name: Object Relations Theory
one_line_summary: Psychoanalytic school focusing on internalized representations of self and others.
band_notes: Influential in clinical psychoanalysis; not amenable to standard empirical validation.

name: Self Psychology
one_line_summary: Kohut's psychoanalytic framework centered on selfobject experiences and narcissistic development.
band_notes: Influential in clinical psychoanalysis; not amenable to standard empirical validation.

name: Heuristics and Biases Program
one_line_summary: Kahneman and Tversky's research program cataloguing systematic deviations from rational judgment.

name: Prospect Theory
one_line_summary: Kahneman and Tversky's account of decision under risk featuring loss aversion and reference dependence.

name: Cognitive Reframing
one_line_summary: Deliberately reinterpreting an event to alter its emotional charge.

name: Thought Records
one_line_summary: CBT worksheet for identifying and challenging automatic thoughts.

name: Behavioral Activation
one_line_summary: Increasing engagement with rewarding activities to interrupt depressive cycles.

name: Mindfulness Practice
one_line_summary: Sustained non-judgmental attention to present experience.
band_notes: Originally Buddhist contemplative practice; now substantial empirical base in clinical contexts (MBSR, MBCT).

name: Box Breathing
one_line_summary: Inhale, hold, exhale, hold for equal counts to regulate the nervous system.

name: Loving-Kindness Meditation
one_line_summary: Buddhist practice cultivating benevolence toward self, loved ones, neutral parties, and difficult people.

name: Journaling
one_line_summary: Regular expressive writing for self-reflection and emotional processing.

name: Morning Pages
one_line_summary: Cameron's daily three pages of stream-of-consciousness longhand writing.

name: Gratitude Journaling
one_line_summary: Regular practice of recording things one is grateful for, linked to wellbeing outcomes.

name: EMDR
one_line_summary: Shapiro's bilateral-stimulation protocol for trauma processing.
band_notes: Empirical support for trauma processing; the specific role of bilateral stimulation as the active mechanism remains debated.

name: Structural Functionalism
one_line_summary: Society as an integrated system of parts each serving stability-maintaining functions.

name: Conflict Theory
one_line_summary: Society as an arena of struggle between groups over scarce resources and power, rooted in Marx.

name: Symbolic Interactionism
one_line_summary: Mead and Blumer's view of society as constituted through meaning-laden interaction.

name: Goffman's Dramaturgy
one_line_summary: Social life analyzed as theatrical performance with frontstage and backstage regions.

name: Bourdieu's Habitus
one_line_summary: Practice as the product of habitus, field, and forms of capital — economic, cultural, social.

name: Foucault's Power-Knowledge
one_line_summary: Power and knowledge as inseparable, jointly producing subjects through discourse and discipline.

name: Weber's Bureaucracy
one_line_summary: Ideal-type bureaucracy characterized by hierarchy, rules, impersonality, and technical expertise.

name: Structuration Theory
one_line_summary: Giddens' account of structure and agency as recursively constituted.

name: Actor-Network Theory
one_line_summary: Latour and Callon's framework treating humans and non-humans as symmetric actants in networks.

name: Critical Theory
one_line_summary: Marxist-derived tradition critiquing culture, ideology, and instrumental rationality.

name: Social Construction of Reality
one_line_summary: Berger and Luckmann's account of how shared meanings come to feel objectively given.

name: Strength of Weak Ties
one_line_summary: Granovetter's finding that loose acquaintances bridge networks more effectively than close ties.

name: Social Capital Theory
one_line_summary: Putnam's framework of bonding, bridging, and linking ties as productive resources.

name: Looking-Glass Self
one_line_summary: Cooley's account of self formed through perception of how others see us.

name: Strain Theory
one_line_summary: Merton's framework of deviance arising from gap between cultural goals and legitimate means.

name: Labeling Theory
one_line_summary: Deviance as a social product of labeling rather than an inherent property of acts.

name: Risk Society
one_line_summary: Beck's account of late modernity as organized around manufactured risks rather than scarcity.

name: Liquid Modernity
one_line_summary: Bauman's framework characterizing the present as fluid, individualized, and unsettled.

name: World-Systems Theory
one_line_summary: Wallerstein's framework of core, periphery, and semi-periphery in the global capitalist system.

name: Theory of Communicative Action
one_line_summary: Habermas' framework distinguishing instrumental from communicative rationality.

name: Virtue Ethics
one_line_summary: Ethics centered on character traits and human flourishing rather than rules or consequences.

name: Deontology
one_line_summary: Ethics grounded in duty and universalizable maxims, independent of consequences.

name: Consequentialism
one_line_summary: Moral worth of action determined by its outcomes; utilitarianism is its most influential variant.

name: Utilitarianism
one_line_summary: Maximize aggregate well-being; classical (Bentham, Mill) and contemporary variants.

name: Contractualism
one_line_summary: Scanlon's view that moral principles are those no one could reasonably reject.

name: Veil of Ignorance
one_line_summary: Choose principles of justice without knowing your own position in society.

name: Capability Approach
one_line_summary: Sen and Nussbaum's framework evaluating well-being by what people can do and be.

name: Care Ethics
one_line_summary: Gilligan and Noddings' framework grounding ethics in relationships and responsiveness rather than abstract principle.

name: Pragmatism
one_line_summary: Peirce, James, Dewey: meaning and truth grounded in practical consequences and inquiry.

name: Existentialism
one_line_summary: Existence precedes essence; meaning is created through choice, freedom, and responsibility.

name: Phenomenology
one_line_summary: Husserl's method of describing structures of conscious experience as they appear.

name: Hermeneutics
one_line_summary: Theory and practice of interpretation, especially of texts and historical understanding.

name: Stoicism
one_line_summary: Hellenistic philosophy emphasizing virtue, reason, and acceptance of what one cannot control.

name: Epicureanism
one_line_summary: Hellenistic philosophy seeking tranquility through prudent pleasure and absence of pain.

name: Falsificationism
one_line_summary: Popper's criterion that scientific claims must be capable of being proven wrong.

name: Paradigm Shift
one_line_summary: Kuhn's account of science as alternating periods of normal science and revolutionary change.

name: Lakatosian Research Programmes
one_line_summary: Lakatos' refinement of Popper: programmes have hard cores and protective belts of auxiliary hypotheses.

name: Bayesian Epistemology
one_line_summary: Belief modeled as probability and updated by Bayes' rule on new evidence.
band_notes: Distinct from Bayesian Inference (formal-scientific); this is the philosophical position that belief should be modeled probabilistically.

name: Reflective Equilibrium
one_line_summary: Iterative adjustment between principles and considered judgments until coherence is reached.

name: Foundationalism
one_line_summary: Knowledge structure resting on basic non-inferentially justified beliefs.

name: Coherentism
one_line_summary: Knowledge justified by mutual support among beliefs, with no privileged foundation.

name: Reliabilism
one_line_summary: Knowledge as belief produced by reliable cognitive processes.

name: Occam's Razor
one_line_summary: Among competing hypotheses, prefer the one with fewest assumptions.

name: Hanlon's Razor
one_line_summary: Never attribute to malice that which is adequately explained by stupidity.

name: Sturgeon's Law
one_line_summary: Ninety percent of everything is crud — used to push past surface dismissal.

name: Steelmanning
one_line_summary: Construct the strongest possible version of an opposing argument before engaging it.

name: First Principles Thinking
one_line_summary: Decomposing a problem to its foundational truths and reasoning upward.

name: Principle of Charity
one_line_summary: Interpret others' arguments in their strongest plausible form.

name: Trolley Problem
one_line_summary: Foot and Thomson's thought experiment probing intuitions about killing vs letting die.

name: Ship of Theseus
one_line_summary: Thought experiment about identity through gradual replacement of parts.

name: Veil of Ignorance Method
one_line_summary: Reasoning device for fairness by stripping knowledge of one's own position.

name: Separation of Powers
one_line_summary: Montesquieu's division of state authority among legislative, executive, and judicial branches.

name: Federalism
one_line_summary: Sovereignty divided constitutionally between national and subnational governments.

name: Public Choice Theory
one_line_summary: Buchanan and Tullock applying economic methods to political behavior.

name: Median Voter Theorem
one_line_summary: Under single-peaked preferences and majority rule, the median voter's preference wins.

name: Arrow's Impossibility Theorem
one_line_summary: No rank-order voting system can satisfy a small set of fairness criteria simultaneously.

name: Realism (IR)
one_line_summary: International relations driven by states pursuing power in an anarchic system.

name: Liberalism (IR)
one_line_summary: International relations shaped by institutions, interdependence, and democratic norms.

name: Constructivism (IR)
one_line_summary: International behavior shaped by socially constructed identities and norms.

name: Democratic Peace Theory
one_line_summary: Empirical regularity that mature democracies rarely fight one another.

name: Soft Power
one_line_summary: Nye's concept of influence through attraction and persuasion rather than coercion.

name: Smart Power
one_line_summary: Combining hard and soft power instruments contextually.

name: Overton Window
one_line_summary: The range of policy ideas considered politically acceptable at a given time.

name: Spiral of Silence
one_line_summary: Noelle-Neumann's account of opinion suppression when people perceive themselves in a minority.

name: Agenda-Setting Theory
one_line_summary: Media doesn't tell us what to think but powerfully shapes what to think about.

name: Iron Triangle
one_line_summary: Stable policy alliances among legislators, agencies, and interest groups.

name: Hegemonic Stability Theory
one_line_summary: International economic openness depends on a dominant state willing to provide public goods.

name: Just War Theory
one_line_summary: Conditions under which war is morally justified, divided into jus ad bellum and jus in bello.
band_notes: Theological roots in Augustine and Aquinas; contemporary scholarship is largely secular philosophical.

name: Two-Level Games
one_line_summary: Putnam's model of international negotiation as simultaneous play at domestic and international tables.

name: REST
one_line_summary: Fielding's architectural style for distributed hypermedia systems.

name: ACID Properties
one_line_summary: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability — guarantees for reliable transactions.

name: BASE Properties
one_line_summary: Basically Available, Soft state, Eventual consistency — pragmatic alternative to ACID.

name: CAP Theorem
one_line_summary: Distributed system can guarantee at most two of consistency, availability, partition tolerance.

name: PACELC Theorem
one_line_summary: Extension of CAP: even without partitions, systems trade latency against consistency.

name: Domain-Driven Design
one_line_summary: Evans' approach aligning software model with domain language and bounded contexts.

name: Event-Driven Architecture
one_line_summary: System organized around production, detection, and reaction to events.

name: CQRS
one_line_summary: Separates read and write models for scalability and clarity.

name: Event Sourcing
one_line_summary: Persist state as an immutable sequence of events rather than current snapshots.

name: Hexagonal Architecture

name: Show Don't Tell
one_line_summary: Craft principle preferring scene and sensory detail over exposition.

name: In Medias Res
one_line_summary: Beginning a narrative in the middle of action rather than at the chronological start.

name: Neuro-Linguistic Programming
one_line_summary: Bandler and Grinder's framework linking neurology, language, and patterned behavior; widely used in coaching despite weak empirical support.
band_notes: Cultural penetration is high; specific claims about modeling excellence and neural correlates have been disconfirmed in mainstream cognitive science.

name: Spiral Dynamics
one_line_summary: Beck and Cowan's value-systems hierarchy adapted from Graves' research, used in organizational and developmental contexts.
band_notes: Adapted from Clare Graves' work but Graves himself never published comprehensive empirical validation; no peer-reviewed validation of the value-meme hierarchy.

name: Integral Theory
one_line_summary: Wilber's metasystematic synthesis integrating quadrants, levels, lines, states, and types of human development.
band_notes: Influential in transpersonal psychology and integral studies; not empirically validated and explicitly questions empirical validation as sole criterion of truth.

name: Pomodoro Technique
one_line_summary: Cirillo's time-management technique using 25-minute focus intervals separated by short breaks.

name: Basel III
one_line_summary: Bank capital, leverage, and liquidity standards from the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision, post-2008.
band_notes: Implemented through national regulators with local variation; Basel IV finalization is in progress.

name: CAMELS Rating
one_line_summary: US bank examination rating: Capital, Assets, Management, Earnings, Liquidity, Sensitivity to market risk.

name: Dodd-Frank Act
one_line_summary: US 2010 financial reform legislation establishing CFPB, FSOC, Volcker Rule, and resolution authority.

name: BSA/AML
one_line_summary: US framework requiring financial institutions to detect and report suspicious activity.

name: KYC
one_line_summary: Customer due diligence requirements identifying who is doing business with a financial institution.

name: Community Reinvestment Act
one_line_summary: US 1977 law requiring banks to meet credit needs of all communities they serve, including low-income areas.

name: FFIEC IT Examination Handbook
one_line_summary: Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council guidance for examining IT operations at supervised institutions.

name: CCAR
one_line_summary: Federal Reserve's annual capital adequacy assessment of large bank holding companies.

name: DFAST
one_line_summary: Annual stress testing required for banks above asset thresholds under Dodd-Frank.

name: CECL
one_line_summary: US GAAP standard requiring forward-looking estimation of expected credit losses over instrument lifetime.

name: IFRS 9
one_line_summary: International accounting standard for financial instruments, including expected credit loss model.

name: ALCO Framework
one_line_summary: Bank governance framework for managing interest rate risk, liquidity, and balance sheet structure.
band_notes: Conceptual governance framework rather than a codified standard; specific structure varies considerably across institutions.

name: Sarbanes-Oxley
one_line_summary: US 2002 law mandating financial reporting controls and executive certifications for public companies.

name: COSO Internal Control-Integrated Framework
one_line_summary: Five-component framework for designing internal controls: control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information and communication, monitoring.

name: COSO ERM
one_line_summary: Enterprise-level extension of COSO internal control framework integrating strategy and performance with risk.

name: ISO 31000
one_line_summary: International standard providing principles and generic guidelines on risk management.

name: Three Lines Model
one_line_summary: IIA framework distinguishing operational management, risk and compliance functions, and internal audit assurance.
band_notes: 2020 IIA update renamed and refined the older 'Three Lines of Defense' framing; conceptual framework rather than a codified standard.

name: FAIR
one_line_summary: Quantitative risk framework decomposing risk into loss event frequency and loss magnitude with probabilistic factors.
band_notes: Quantitative methodology now standardized as Open FAIR through The Open Group; distinct from qualitative risk-rating approaches.

name: ORSA
one_line_summary: Insurance-sector self-assessment of all material risks against capital and solvency.

name: NIST Cybersecurity Framework
one_line_summary: Six core functions (Govern, Identify, Protect, Detect, Respond, Recover) plus implementation tiers and profiles.

name: NIST 800-53
one_line_summary: Catalog of security and privacy controls for federal information systems and organizations.

name: NIST Risk Management Framework
one_line_summary: Seven-step process for integrating security, privacy, and risk management into the system development lifecycle.

name: ISO/IEC 27001
one_line_summary: International standard specifying requirements for an information security management system (ISMS).

name: ISO/IEC 27002
one_line_summary: International standard providing guidance on information security controls.

name: CIS Controls
one_line_summary: Center for Internet Security's prioritized set of cybersecurity actions for organizations.

name: MITRE ATT&CK
one_line_summary: Globally accessible knowledge base of adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures based on real-world observations.
band_notes: Knowledge base structure rather than a prescriptive control framework; widely used as reference and threat-modeling input.

name: Cyber Kill Chain
one_line_summary: Seven-phase model of intrusion: reconnaissance, weaponization, delivery, exploitation, installation, command-and-control, actions on objectives.
band_notes: Lockheed Martin's framework biases toward perimeter-centric thinking; less aligned with cloud and zero-trust architectures.

name: Diamond Model of Intrusion Analysis
one_line_summary: Four-feature framework for intrusion events: adversary, capability, infrastructure, victim.

name: STRIDE
one_line_summary: Microsoft threat modeling categorization: Spoofing, Tampering, Repudiation, Information disclosure, Denial of service, Elevation of privilege.

name: PASTA
aliases: Process for Attack Simulation and Threat Analysis
one_line_summary: Seven-stage risk-centric threat modeling methodology.

name: Zero Trust Architecture
one_line_summary: Security model assuming no implicit trust based on network location; every access decision is verified.
band_notes: Coined by Forrester's John Kindervag; codified into NIST 800-207 for operational guidance.

name: Defense in Depth
one_line_summary: Strategy using multiple overlapping security controls so failure of any single layer does not compromise the system.

name: CMMC
one_line_summary: DoD certification framework for protecting federal contract information and controlled unclassified information.

name: HITRUST CSF
one_line_summary: Certifiable framework integrating HIPAA, NIST, ISO, PCI, and other authoritative sources.

name: FedRAMP
aliases: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program
one_line_summary: US government program standardizing security assessment and authorization for cloud services.

name: PCI DSS
aliases: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard
one_line_summary: Industry standard for organizations handling branded credit cards from major card networks.

name: GDPR
one_line_summary: EU regulation on data protection and privacy applicable to processing of EU residents' personal data.
band_notes: Has substantial extraterritorial reach; non-EU organizations processing EU residents' data must comply.

name: CCPA
one_line_summary: California state law granting consumers rights over personal information collected by businesses.

name: HIPAA
aliases: Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act
one_line_summary: US law establishing privacy and security standards for protected health information.

name: Privacy by Design
one_line_summary: Cavoukian's seven foundational principles for embedding privacy into the design of systems and processes.

name: FIPPs
one_line_summary: Foundational set of principles (notice, choice, access, security, accountability) underlying most privacy regimes.

name: Differential Privacy
one_line_summary: Formal definition guaranteeing that the inclusion or exclusion of any single record does not significantly affect query outputs.

name: ISO 9001
one_line_summary: International standard for quality management systems with seven principles including process approach and continuous improvement.

name: ITIL
one_line_summary: Framework for IT service management including service strategy, design, transition, operation, and continual improvement.

name: COBIT
aliases: Control Objectives for Information and Related Technologies
one_line_summary: ISACA framework for governance and management of enterprise IT.

name: TOGAF
one_line_summary: Enterprise architecture framework with Architecture Development Method (ADM) and content metamodel.

name: Zachman Framework
one_line_summary: Enterprise architecture taxonomy intersecting six perspectives with six abstractions (what, how, where, who, when, why).

name: CMMI
one_line_summary: Five-level process maturity model: Initial, Managed, Defined, Quantitatively Managed, Optimizing.

name: SOC 2
one_line_summary: AICPA framework for reporting on controls relevant to security, availability, processing integrity, confidentiality, and privacy.

name: SSAE 18
one_line_summary: Statement on Standards for Attestation Engagements 18 — current AICPA standard governing service organization audits.

name: TCFD
aliases: Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures
one_line_summary: Voluntary framework for climate-related financial risk disclosures across governance, strategy, risk, and metrics.

name: SASB
one_line_summary: Industry-specific sustainability disclosure standards, now under the IFRS Foundation's ISSB.

name: GRI
one_line_summary: Most widely used sustainability reporting framework with universal, sector, and topic standards.

name: LEED
aliases: Leadership in Energy and Environmental Design
one_line_summary: USGBC certification system for green buildings across categories like energy, water, materials, and indoor environment.
